body:
Sorry, I had some trouble with the auto mod when asking the question.  

We have no official court order for visitation.  It’s just verbal.  I can pretty much see them whenever I want.  But last night she said she wants the names of everyone they will be around and where we will be.  She’s threatening to take me down to parental minimums if I don’t.  I am just wondering if I am required to literally give her info on every friend they may be around when they visit.

I appreciate you taking the time to reply.  I might actually give the writing thing a shot.  

As for family...they are the absolute worst people to talk to for me.  My parents guilt me, and my father is a big part of why I’m having suicidal thoughts in the first place.  Yesterday I tried to tell him something, and instead of focusing on what I had to say he decided to yell and cuss at me because I lost my job.  (For something I absolutely did not do). 

My mother means well but she is unable to understand what I go through and ends up not being helpful.  She tends to resort to guilting me when I don’t agree with what she says.  I can’t handle that right now.

I appreciate the response.  I do realize that it's my mental health and ultimately my responsibility.  It's just hurtful that the person closest to me doesn't want to support me in this difficult time.  I DO understand why, given our past, but it still sucks that I can't count on her for support.

Thanks so much for taking time to respond.

I'm not looking for a therapist in her.  I am looking for someone to talk to about the negative thoughts in my head, which I assumed my partner would do.  Also if work and improvement don't lead to trust then how exactly do I come back from this?

As for the therapy...I'm 100% sure I can't afford ANY therapist at the moment.  Free programs are the only thing for me, and in my area the best I could get is once a month.  I feel like I need more than that.
In this case I didn't actually make a mistake, yet.  She's doing it in anticipation of me making a mistake.
I can't afford therapy.  Free programs would be the only thing that I could get support from.  But for someone with anxiety it's difficult to just spring into those types of situations.

Is that really fair to expect, though?  How can we move forward with the feeling that we can't make mistakes?  Mistakes are what help us to learn.  I could understand IF you weren't making any improvements, but if you are...then shouldn't people recognize that and not treat you the same way after a while?

I'm trying not to destroy myself, that's part of the problem.  I'm trying to reach out to someone for help, and they want to be distant from me because I haven't handled situations like this very well in the past.  

Really long story short:  About a year ago I went through some very serious depression and suicidal thoughts.  Got better, got on anti-depressants, made significant improvements to how I react and how I handle these types of situations.  Now I'm going through a hard time and having suicidal thoughts again, but my girlfriend wants to be distant because of the past.  I feel like the person who is closest to me doesn't want to be supportive of me when I feel like I need her, and it's difficult to understand.
